obligations.obligation: must_include: The two maps as objects and the void-roads convention shown through Cael's cataloguing (dashes ending in nothing versus ruts; the carter's three circles); Karis's line about the two maps verbatim.
obligations.evidence: The registry sheet as object and convention: 'A road east of the Line on a registry sheet was a row of dashes that thinned as if the pen had been lifting, and stopped in white paper, and the white went to the edge of the sheet. Seven roads left the Line going east on the printed sheet, and every one of them ended in nothing. / That was the void style. ... a road drawn in the void style was a road the registry would not vouch for.' The catalogue: 'Ink: a dash the width of a pen, a gap, a dash. Ground: a road two carts wide at the wash and one on the rises, rutted to the depth of his hand ... Ink: nothing at the end. Ground: Lowmarch behind him with a ferry and a board and thirteen crews on a wall ... The dashes were not a lie. They were where the registry had stopped being willing to say so.' The carter's map: 'A carter's map. No seal, no brand, no waystation at either end of anything ... And three times he had counted a road on Pike's map go out of true. Bent, as a road bends round a bog, and came back to its line a finger's width on. Inside each bend the carter's hand had drawn a circle with nothing in it.' Karis verbatim: 'Karis had watched him look from one sheet to the other four times, and had waited for the fifth, and said: "Their map has no roads. His has no quiet ground. Between them you get the country."'

obligations.obligation: must_include: Oryn at Thornwater's gate on the ninth day; her two reasons in her register (the still-and-whole patient; the carters' claim about a healer's hands, 'before somebody bleeds on the wrong side of it'); her eleven times past the line; six on the road; the crew added to her route, not the reverse.
obligations.evidence: At the gate: 'And at the gate itself, tied to the post, a second mule, with panniers, and a bench pulled into the wall's shade, and a woman on the bench with a carter's hand in both of hers.' Ninth day: '"Ninth day. I said nine. You've counted." / "Ninety-third." / "Then that's both of us."' Reason one: '"Two reasons. I'll give you both, because you'll count them anyway. The first is a patient I want to read whole and still. The long one. That wants a day of him not fighting anything, and I've not had one of those with him yet, and I'll not get one on my route, because my route's a table and a road and a table. So I'm putting one on it. A day."' Reason two: '"Every carter on this road will tell you a healer's hands stop working on quiet ground. Every one. Not the sigil. The hands. ... I've walked past that line on the Fallow road eleven times in two years. I've never once had a reason to put my hands on anybody at it, and nobody's ever bled at it in front of me, so I've never been able to check. I'd like to know if that's true before somebody bleeds on the wrong side of it."' Never off the road: '"I've never stepped off the road there. Never wanted to."' Crew added to her route: '"You're a stop. I've added you. Two days east is on my route as far as the bend. Past the bend it isn't, and a day standing at it isn't, and that's a day I'll owe at the next hold, and I've been late there before. Don't make it a long stop."' Six on the road, stated once and not underlined: 'Six on the Fallow road out of Thornwater's east gate on the morning of the ninety-fourth, in the order the road set: ...'

obligations.obligation: must_include: Ephram's letter, in full: the Crown yard's new cohort captain; Withrow's tenure holding; the registry query about 'former enrollees' last known direction of travel' answered by Bracken with a map reference to the Line and nothing past it — 'which is true, and which Bracken enjoyed being true'; and the line Cael reads three times.
obligations.evidence: Letter composed in Ephram's register around the fixed facts, italicized as in-world writing: '*The Crown yard has a new cohort captain. The intake came up the bluff a fortnight ago, forty-one of them, and they've put a third-year over them who was a second-year when you left and whose name you would not know, so I'll not spend the ink.*' '*Withrow's tenure holds. That is the whole of the sentence.*' '*A query came down to the registry from somewhere above it. Bracken would not say where and I did not ask twice. It wanted former enrollees' last known direction of travel. Bracken answered it. He gave them a map reference to the Line and nothing past it — which is true, and which Bracken enjoyed being true.*' Fixed final line: '*Rooke says the yard's quieter. He didn't say it was worse. He also didn't say it wasn't.*' Read three times: 'He read the last line three times. / Once for what it said, which was a sentence about a yard. Once for what it did not say, which was more, and left out on purpose. The third time because it was last.' Only Halcenvane, Withrow, Bracken, Rooke are named in connection with the letter; the new captain is deliberately unnamed in Ephram's own words.

'*Filed with your record. It reads: left in good standing, undefeated on paper. I've kept this ledger forty years and never had a line like it. The session still stands. The road still runs through Ardenmere. — V.*' Carried as an object: 'A strip of ledger paper, cut straight along the rule with a knife, folded once.' Read aloud to Lira on the Fallow road; 'the session still stands' filed as unexplained: 'He did not know what *the session still stands* meant. He knew it was not nothing, because she had spent a line of ledger paper on it, and he put it on the shelf as it was, unexplained.'

obligations.obligation: must_include: The last mile staged in the body before the mind: the four spoken reactions verbatim (Lira, Brom, Karis; Seln's procedure), Oryn's silent half-raised hands, the ten paces back, the stone.
obligations.evidence: Body first: 'Lira stopped. / Her hand came up as it had come up on the first walk out of Thornwater ... and stayed up.' Then: '"It's like the air got thick," she said.' Brom: 'the shoulders, which did not move for anything, moved, once ... "Like a door closing behind me," Brom said.' Oryn: 'her hands came up. Half up. Not to her face and not to anything; to the height she raised them over a hurt before they went down on it, and she held them there, open, over nothing, and did not say anything at all.' Karis: '"My Arbiter's gone," Karis said. / Precise. Four words, said over an instrument.' 'Everyone stopped.' Seln: '"Back up. Ten paces. Tell me when it comes back."' The ten paces and the line: 'On the third stride back Brom said, "Back," ... and Karis, on her third, at the same place on the road, said, "Back"; and Seln ... said it on his fourth, which was the same place; and Lira ... said it when she came level with the others, on the same ground, to the stride.' '"Ten," Seln said, and they went to ten, because the procedure was ten, and stood.' The stone: 'Then she walked forward, to the place, and not one step past it, and bent, and took up a stone from the road's edge the size of two fists, and set it in the rut at her heel, on the near side.'

obligations.obligation: must_include: Cael feels nothing change and says nothing; the mid-chapter log entry verbatim.
obligations.evidence: At the stride: 'He looked at the place. Dark. The same dark, exactly, unchanged in any way he had a word for. Nothing had gone from it, because nothing had been in it. Nine fragments, held to nothing: nothing drifting, nothing different. The air was not thick. No door had closed. He stood on the road beside Karis, at the stride where four people had felt a thing, and he felt nothing change, and he did not say so.' On the way out: 'He had backed up ten paces on a road with five people who had felt a thing stop and start, and he had felt nothing stop and nothing start, in either direction, and nobody had asked him. ... he looked for the reason and found two: he did not know what it meant, and nobody had asked.' The log, mid-chapter (a full section of prose follows it), with a dateline line in the established convention: '*Ninety-fifth day. The Fallow road, second day east of Thornwater; the rise, the bend, the shoulder. A hundred and eight in hand; nothing owed. A stone in a rut.* / *Quiet ground. Karis's Arbiter stopped at a line she can mark with a rock. So did Lira's, Brom's, Seln's, Oryn's — same line, same step. Mine didn't. Mine's been stopped since I was fourteen. I don't know what that means. Nobody asked. Tomorrow we go in.*'

obligations.obligation: must_include: The chapter ENDS on the image (the ring in the last light; Oryn lowering her hands) — not on the log.
obligations.evidence: Final paragraphs: 'Past the ridge the ground fell away and opened, a shallow bowl of short grey grass, and in the bowl, off the road, a long stone's throw and more, there were the stones Pike had said. Some standing. Uprights, broken, most of them, at different heights, as teeth are broken, in a ring ... And under them, a floor. ... the floor took the light as water takes it, all of it at once, bright along its whole width, so that the ring of broken uprights stood on a pool of light with the dusk already in the grass around it.' Last line of the file: 'She held her hands out over the line for as long as the floor held the sun, and when it had gone off the floor and there was only the ridge lit, and then not even that, she lowered them.' Scene-closer: IMAGE (Chapter 8 closed on a log entry; no repeat).

obligations.obligation: payoff: Pike's 'Your Arbiter tells you. It stops.' paid at the stride.

Paid: '"My Arbiter's gone," Karis said.' and 'Pike had said they would know. Five of them had known, at a stride, and had known again, at the same stride, going the other way.' The payoff is inverted for Cael in the same beat: his Arbiter tells him nothing, because it has nothing to stop.

inventions: Timeline: the slip marked at the plank on the morning of the NINETY-FIRST day and the five leave Lowmarch the same morning; a noon halt at the wash on the ninety-second (Ephram's letter read); Thornwater reached on the afternoon of the NINETY-THIRD (Oryn at the gate; her table till dark; the crew in the grain loft); six leave by Thornwater's east gate on the morning of the NINETY-FOURTH (Vell's letter read at the noon halt); the rise, the bend, and the line reached in the hour before dusk on the NINETY-FIFTH; camp on the road on the near side of the stone, no fire. Cael is eighteen (not restated on the page this chapter; no age reference given).

The monthly mail sack arrives on the ferry on the morning of the ninety-first (a month after Chapter 4's sack on the sixtieth) and is sorted aloud at the plank: twenty-two pieces, the last two for Cael. Both letters are carried unopened off the landing and read on the walk.

The registry's printed continental sheet (the wall map of every registry office, the Weaver's Row schoolroom, and Ilsev's desk) is in Karis's middle box among her copies of registry print; Cael walks with it open from Lowmarch to Thornwater and returns it to the box at Thornwater's east gate because the Fallow road is not on it at all — the surveyors' dashes stop at Thornwater's fork and the sheet is white east of it. Seven dashed roads leave the Line going east on the sheet; the Lowmarch–Thornwater road is the third from the Line. The void style's rule as Cael learned it at Ilsev's desk: a road drawn in the void style is a road the registry will not vouch for.

Karis finished copying Pike's plank map whole on the morning of the ninety-first while the slip was marked (she had copied the Fallow road's bend on the ninetieth). The copy is a carter's map: no seal, no brand, roads solid and not straight; three roads go out of true round three circles drawn blank; one of the three is the Fallow road's second-day bend.

Ephram's letter: composed in his register (plain, in order, the deciding line last). Invented details around the fixed facts: the intake of forty-one came up the bluff a fortnight before; the new cohort captain is a third-year who was a second-year when Cael left, deliberately unnamed by Ephram ('I'll not spend the ink'); Withrow's tenure held after a week in which 'there had been' a longer sentence; Bracken told Ephram about the query at the plaque wall with his hands behind his back and then told him he had not told him; Ephram still loses their bout to Cael 'every time I run it' and has stopped running it in the yard. Signed '— E.' No date. Ephram knows nothing of the mechanism and says nothing of it.

Vell's letter is written on a strip of her own ledger paper cut along the rule, folded once — the first piece of that paper Cael has ever held that was his. He reads it aloud to Lira at the noon halt on the Fallow road; Lira's reading of it: '"On paper,"' / '"The road still runs through Ardenmere. She put that last."' / Cael: '"She puts the thing that decides it last."' / Lira: '"So does Ephram."'

Thornwater's gate on the ninety-third: the same bowman on the gate-walk (Chapter 3's), who calls nothing down; a bench in the wall's shade where Oryn runs a surface reading on a carter's hand (a count of ten; 'keep it dry and you'll not lift with it for six days'); her mule tied to the gate-post. She looks the five over as patients (Lira's leg — a nod; Brom's forearm — nothing; Karis's hands — a count of one; Seln — nothing; Cael's tape through the shirt — 'Seventeen days.' / 'Breath stops at it.' / 'It'll do that till it's off.'). She does NOT read Cael (no fourth surface reading; count unchanged at three). She knows where the crew is going because a carter who was at the plank when the slip was marked came into Thornwater the day before.

Oryn's table at Thornwater that evening, watched by Cael from the loft door: nine on the bench in the order she set (a child with a wrist first; then the three that mattered; then the rest); one sit-down between the fourth and fifth; nobody asks her for paper or tier. Her route arithmetic in her words: the Fallow road east of Thornwater is on her route as far as the bend; past the bend is not; a day at the bend is a day she will owe at the next hold (unnamed, a brand on Pike's map past the bend), where she has been late before. Twelve times past the line after this walk.

Order of march on the Fallow road: Seln out of sight ahead; Lira twenty paces on; Brom with two boxes by strap; the third box on Oryn's mule; Oryn on the mule's down-slope side; Karis with the carter's map; Cael. Oryn's walking catalogued: economical, sure-footed, never fast; does not look at the ground, does not look back, stops when the mule stops. Lira looks back at her twice in the first hour and then stops looking.

The last mile: the road climbs out of thinning scrub (waist to knee to grass and stone) to a low ridge running across the road's line, with a shoulder to the left where the road bends hard left round it and out of sight; the calf says nine on the climb; the ribs stop his breath at the tape. Seln comes back down the road at the foot of the rise and takes the rear without a word. Lira sets her own lead at six paces. The line crosses the road at the shoulder's foot, where the road begins to leave its line — on the road, as Pike's folklore has it ('a place on it where your Arbiter stops').

The line found on the way out, not by re-entry: each Arbiter returns at the same place on the road (Brom and Karis on their third stride back, Seln on his fourth from a pace further in, Lira when she comes level from six paces further in); Oryn gives Seln one nod at that place with her hands still up and does not speak; Cael says nothing and nobody asks him. Karis walks forward to the place and not one step past it and sets a two-fist stone in the rut at her heel on the near side. The procedure is completed to ten paces as Seln said.

Camp: on the road, on the near (Thornwater) side of the stone, at Seln's word; no fire, at Seln's word, unquestioned 'because Pike had said where the dogs lived'. Brom sets the three boxes on the Thornwater side of the stone. Lira re-tapes the ankle. Seln stands at the stone and goes no further. Karis writes a short entry Cael reads as a stride, not a hypothesis. Nobody passes the stone.

The view from the stone at dusk, limited to what is visible from the line: past the ridge, a shallow bowl of short grey grass; off the road, 'a long stone's throw and more', a ring of broken uprights of different heights ('as teeth are broken'), uncounted; under them a floor that takes the last sun 'as water takes it', a pool of light with dusk in the grass around it. No fused stone, no lip, no carvings, no measurement, no colour of the stone, no count of the uprights.
Cael's shelf of kept sentences gains Karis's 'Between them you get the country' (filed beside 'sixty-four'), Vell's 'undefeated on paper', and Ephram's last line.
state_change_proposals: Timeline: Lowmarch left on the NINETY-FIRST day past the Line after the recovery slip was marked at the plank (HOLD, five names) in front of the meadow; Thornwater reached on the afternoon of the NINETY-THIRD; six leave Thornwater's east gate on the NINETY-FOURTH; the line at the Fallow road's second-day bend reached in the hour before dusk on the NINETY-FIFTH; camp that night on the road at the stone. Cael is eighteen (no age reference on the page this chapter). The mandated 'Tomorrow we go in' places Chapter 10's morning on the NINETY-SIXTH day.

Party SIX from Thornwater's east gate on the ninety-fourth: Cael, Lira, Brom, Karis, Seln, Oryn. Oryn has NOT joined; she has added the crew to her route as a stop ('You're a stop. I've added you.'), stated in her words at Thornwater's gate; the Fallow road is on her route as far as the bend; past the bend is not; a day at the bend is a day she owes at the next hold (unnamed), where she has been late before. Her count past the Fallow Ring's line: eleven times in two years before this walk; 'Twelve in two days' — after this chapter, twelve. She has never stepped off the road there and said so.

Oryn's two reasons, on the page in her words: (1) 'a patient I want to read whole and still. The long one. That wants a day of him not fighting anything ... So I'm putting one on it. A day.' (2) 'Every carter on this road will tell you a healer's hands stop working on quiet ground. ... I'd like to know if that's true before somebody bleeds on the wrong side of it.' She has never been able to check the carters' claim; it remains unchecked at chapter end (no hands on anyone at the line).

Letters received on the ninety-first (the monthly ferry sack, twenty-two pieces, sorted aloud at the plank): Ephram's from Halcenvane and Vell's from Ardenmere, both now in Cael's satchel against the leather book. Ephram's text as rendered (in-world, italic): 'Cael — / Weather first, because you'll want it in order, and I've watched you want things in order. / The Crown yard has a new cohort captain. The intake came up the bluff a fortnight ago, forty-one of them, and they've put a third-year over them who was a second-year when you left and whose name you would not know, so I'll not spend the ink. He is fair. He counts slower than you did. They stand where he puts them. / Withrow's tenure holds. That is the whole of the sentence. I asked whether there was a longer one and was told there was not, in a way that meant there had been, for a week. / A query came down to the registry from somewhere above it. Bracken would not say where and I did not ask twice. It wanted former enrollees' last known direction of travel. Bracken answered it. He gave them a map reference to the Line and nothing past it — which is true, and which Bracken enjoyed being true. He told me so at the plaque wall with his hands behind his back, and then told me he had not told me. / I still lose to you every time I run it. I have stopped running it in the yard. / Rooke says the yard's quieter. He didn't say it was worse. He also didn't say it wasn't. / — E.' Vell's text as rendered (verbatim per packet, on a strip of her ledger paper): 'Filed with your record. It reads: left in good standing, undefeated on paper. I've kept this ledger forty years and never had a line like it. The session still stands. The road still runs through Ardenmere. — V.' Knowledge gained: the registry has queried Halcenvane for former enrollees' direction of travel and been answered 'the Line and nothing past it'; Withrow's tenure holds; the Crown yard has a new (unnamed) cohort captain; Vell has filed Cael's resignation as 'left in good standing, undefeated on paper'. 'The session still stands' is filed by Cael as unexplained. No replies written (next westbound ferry a month off).

The maps, now on the page as objects: (a) the registry's printed continental sheet (from Karis's middle box) — roads east of the Line in the void style (dashed, unnamed, unbranded, ending in white); seven such roads leave the Line eastward; the Lowmarch–Thornwater road is the third from the Line; the Fallow road is not on the sheet at all (white east of Thornwater's fork); returned to the box at Thornwater's east gate. (b) Karis's whole copy of Pike's plank map (a carter's map, no seal) — roads solid; three roads bend round three blank circles; one is the Fallow road's second-day bend; Karis carries it on the Fallow road. Karis's sentence on record: 'Their map has no roads. His has no quiet ground. Between them you get the country.'

The line, as known at chapter end (folklore confirmed in the body, nothing more): on the Fallow road, at the foot of the shoulder of the low ridge at the second-day rise, where the road begins to leave its line and bend left; every Arbiter in the party except Cael's stopped at the same place on the road going in and returned at the same place going out (Lira, Brom, Karis, Seln by word; Oryn by a nod with her hands raised); the transition was at a stride; it is marked by a two-fist stone set by Karis in the rut on the near (Thornwater) side. NOT known: size, shape, radius, floor, stakes, mechanism, any theory; the word 'Quieting' does not exist. Nobody has crossed the line since it was marked; nobody has measured anything; Karis's notebook entry is a stride, not a hypothesis.

Cael: nine fragments + anomaly, unchanged; NO deployment; fragments held to nothing on the void road, 'nothing drifting; nothing different' at the line in either direction. His Arbiter: dark before, dark at the line, dark at the tenth pace — 'unchanged in any way he had a word for'. He felt nothing change either direction and SAID NOTHING; nobody asked.
